posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
RMXP comes with a handful of loopable fogs as well! If you own XP, you might be able to repurpose those.
There's a way to make an image tileable in Photoshop and GIMP, it was something about Offset--Offset Image, maybe? I haven't done it in years, I don't remember exactly where it was or what it was called, but I made a lot of use of it when I was doing tiling ground textures for a company I was interning with.
GIMP also has a
"Make Seamless" filter
that does some shenanigans with blurring and repeating parts of the image to make a tiling texture, it looks like--which is kind of weird for an image like the sample but might work really well for a fog!

posts.author: FrigidGaze
posts.body:
On the subject of using GIMP, you can generate a seamless texture right from the getgo without using extra filters on top. Then by tweaking the size and detail you can get something that can be scrolled quite nicely I think. Using Filter > Render > Noise > Solid Noise and ticking tileable.
Then using something like
[Galv's Layer Graphics]
and setting the blend to something like screen, you get a nice fog effect out of the image that loops seamlessly:
I lay out the process in detail so you could potentially make one that suits you more and fits your own game's resolution, but if you use 720p by chance and want the same graphic I whipped up under GIMP's generator I can share it happily. (Or make one that fits the game's resolution if the other options posted didn't suit your needs!)
